findings.claim: splitFrontmatter still does not produce the same result for CRLF input as for the LF equivalent because it preserves carriage returns in the returned front/body.
findings.evidence:
Acceptance criterion `Parsers tolerate CRLF directly` says `parseConf`, `splitFrontmatter`, `routingLayer0` and the line counter SHALL produce the same result for CRLF input as for the LF equivalent; the implementation only changes the delimiter regex to `/^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---?
([\s\S]*)$/`, and the added test explicitly documents `The CRLF input yields CRLF output` before stripping `` for comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize CRLF inside `splitFrontmatter` before returning, or normalize `match[1]` and `match[2]` so the returned `front` and `body` exactly match the LF-input results.

findings.claim: The blocking `no-home-or-tmp-literals` check was changed to depend on `git grep -P`, which the change itself admits may error when PCRE support is unavailable.
findings.evidence: The command policy requires checks to behave the same from `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, bash and zsh; the diff changes the check from `git grep ... -E` to `git grep ... -P`, and the added note says `If a git build lacks PCRE this check errors rather than passing silently`.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the constraint on portable `git grep -E`, or implement the comment-aware filtering in a Node script that is invoked consistently on all supported shells.
